The science, made simple

Pressure sends oxygen where swelling slows it down.

One

Swelling slows the supply

  • Your body repairs with oxygen, and oxygen rides on red blood cells
  • Those cells only reach tissue where blood flows freely
  • Swollen tissue is exactly where they struggle to get through
Two

Pressure changes the rules

  • Inside the chamber, gentle pressure rises
  • Oxygen dissolves directly into the fluid of your blood
  • Not just the cells that carry it
Three

Repair gets its raw material

  • That fluid reaches what red blood cells can't: swollen tissue, incisions, bruised areas
  • Your body gets more of what every repair job runs on

Healing is work. Work takes energy. Your cells make that energy with oxygen.

Hyperbaric oxygen has been used in hospital wound and graft care for decades. This is the same principle, applied to a recovery you chose.

Questions, answered straight

What people ask before booking

When can I start after my procedure?
Decided with Dr. Haas at your consultation, based on your specific procedure and your surgeon's aftercare plan. We coordinate with what your surgeon has already told you, never around it.
Will this interfere with my surgeon's instructions?
No. Compression, rest, wound care and follow-ups stay exactly as prescribed. This is added around them, and we'll tell you if anything conflicts.
What about implants, fillers, drains or compression garments?
That's exactly what the screening covers. Some things need clearing first. You'll get a straight answer before anything is booked beyond the first visit.
Will anyone know?
Your consultation is private. Sessions are an hour lying back in a clear chamber where you can read or nap. There's nothing to hide afterward and nothing added to the downtime you already planned.
What does a session feel like?
You lie back for about an hour. The pressure feels like a plane taking off, then you relax. Our team is right outside the whole time.
How many sessions will I need?
That's what your consultation answers. Most recovery plans run a few sessions a week over two to four weeks.
Does insurance cover this?
No, this is a cash-pay wellness service. Your first visit is $147, and you'll know the full plan and cost before committing to anything more.
